answer: To repel Sybil swarms, agents anchor identity in a cryptographic attestation chain verified by zero-knowledge proofs. To transact past the wharf checkpoint, each node must lock stake inside a shared vault, where collateral requirements scale exponentially (O(2^k)) with each identity cluster. Even if an attacker scatters tokens like wild yarrow across pseudonyms, exponential capital exhaustion renders large-scale network spoofing economically impossible.
